qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Statutory electricity distribution network concessions across Spain alongside a domestic nuclear and renewable fleet. Primary erosion threats include aggressive Spanish political and regulatory intervention (1.2% non-deductible turnover levy, retail gas caps, nuclear production tax hikes), capping returns well below cost of capital.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Spanish integrated utility controlled by Enel (70.1%). While electricity distribution networks are essential, historical ROIC is capped at 6-8%, and Endesa possesses zero pricing power against Spanish state intervention, evidenced by non-deductible 1.2% turnover windfall taxes, inframarginal power caps, and escalating nuclear fuel taxes.
qualitative.evidence: Consolidated ROIC remains range-bound at 6-8%. In 2023-2024, Spanish government levies on top-line revenue (1.2% turnover tax) directly suppressed operating cash flow and NOPAT regardless of profitability. Net debt stands at ~€9.5B. Generation mix faces structural nuclear phase-out costs by 2035 and high regulatory uncertainty in domestic tariff frameworks.
